scope: Current Proposition1 and AppendixJ proof/interpretation; frozen D2 protocol; source-free L issuer and simulation code; existing saved simulation aggregates and TableJ1. No financial or Monte Carlo experiment rerun.

primary_source.title: A strengthened Orlicz-Pettis theorem via Ito-Nisio
primary_source.author: Ethan Sussman
primary_source.actual_reading_scope: Official publisher HTML Proposition3.4, equation3.11, footnote4, and publication metadata reopened in this audit.
primary_source.source_match: Independent symmetric Banach-space-valued summands; scalar specialization valid. The published display uses nonstrict threshold events and R>0; footnote4 discusses strict/nonstrict variants. The supplied scalar first-crossing argument separately handles the strict events and c=0 used in the manuscript.

proof_checks.agreement: Independence makes the remaining sum independent of each finite-history first-crossing event; individual zero-symmetry makes its two closed half-axis probabilities at least one half. Equal summand laws and finite moments are unnecessary.

For c>=0 a first crossing is strictly positive or strictly negative. A remaining sum with the same weak sign keeps the terminal sum strictly beyond c. Residual atoms at zero do not invalidate the half-probability argument. The same proof covers c=0.
For the finite .975 lower quantile q of |S_H|, right continuity yields P(|S_H|>q)<=.025 even at an atom. Since max_h|x+S_h|<=|x|+max_h|S_h|, strict breach of |x|+q has probability at most.05.

The fixed-x population statement is unconditional. A random observed issue anchor becomes fixed only under its issue-information conditional law; the manuscript explicitly requires conditional independence/symmetry and the corresponding conditional endpoint quantile rather than inferring them from unconditional marginals.

Code uses completed origins r-H-W+1 throughr-H, endpoint sample |N[i+H]-N[i]|, rank ceil(39(W+1)/40), then actual |N[t]| plus the frozen endpoint order statistic. This is a declared empirical plugin, not the known population quantile; dependent overlapping changing samples have no inherited population guarantee.

The stated X1=Z, X2=-Z example has symmetric marginals, zero terminal sum and unit maximum, so population q=0 and the strict peak breach is certain. It correctly shows general failure without independence and is separate from the positive-AR experiment.

Code initializes each path increment at N(0,1), then uses independent Gaussian innovations with variance1-phi^2, so marginal increment variance1 and covariance phi^lag hold. The oracle endpoint variance is the sum of that covariance matrix and its absolute .975 quantile uses normal .9875. Starting x=0 makes this an unconditional population-threshold experiment; finite empirical calibration uncertainty is intentionally absent.

Positive phi invalidates the independence premise, but need not violate the numerical bound. All eight retained observed simulation rates are below5%; the manuscript does not treat those finite settings as a general theorem extension, an empirical coverage guarantee or a pinball-risk ordering.

limits: This is a finite source/proof/code-consistency audit, not verification of the financial data law or the empirical calibration quantile.
No claim of conditional independence/symmetry for real FX or Treasury increments was empirically established here.
Saved Monte Carlo aggregate arithmetic was checked, but RNG paths were not regenerated and finite simulation does not prove a universal probability inequality.
Working-reference financial DM/HLN/Holm outputs were outside this proof-focused audit.
No source, financial result, CHANGELOG or registry file was edited.
